Amendment of the Comprehensive Plan for Water & Sewerage Systems, Worcester County, Maryland As the next item of business, the Planning Commission reviewed an application associated to expand water and sewer planning areas for the Ocean Pines Sanitary Service Area in the Master Water and Sewerage Plan (The Plan) for a proposed development on Parcels 130, and 191 of Tax Map 15. Robert Mitchell, Director of Environmental Programs, presented the staff report to the Planning Commission. The applicant is Hugh Cropper on behalf of the owners, the Ocean Pines Partnership. Mr. Mitchell explained that since the owner’s application for rezoning to R-3 was denied, they cannot construct their original number of planned homes (89) and will need to settle for the density allowed by the R-2 zoning which is fifty-nine (59) homes. They will instead plan for a potential utilization of (59) EDUs of public water and sewer from the Ocean Pines Sanitary Service Area to serve the proposed development under the present zoning’s density limit. Mr. Mitchell indicated that this amendment seeks to change the water and sewer planning area designations for the properties from W-6, S-6 (no planned service) to W-1, S-1 (immediate to two years). He mentioned that there are no existing water or onsite sewage systems present on the property as the well and cesspool were abandoned in 2013. Consistencies with both the 2006 and 2026 Worcester County Comprehensive Plan were presented, including the Land Use Designation in both plans. The comments for the Department of Public Works (DPW) were also mentioned, specifically concerning the proposed connection routes to connect to public water and sewer infrastructure in the vicinity of the subject properties. DPW also mentioned that the water extension and force main connection described provide a preliminary basis for engineering feasibility, and any infrastructure must be designed, constructed and operated in accordance with applicable County standards and required permits. Mr. Mitchell closed addressing and email concerning public comments specifically directed for this proposed development. The adequacy of treatment plant capacity, infrastructure capacities for distribution and collection systems, and financial responsibilities of the developer were all addressed before the Planning Commission. He called this a proper planning amendment, a statement which drew agreement from Ms. Wimbrow. Mr. Cropper introduced Mr. Steve Engle, a local development consultant with Vista Design and offered the Commission that Mr. Engle and his firm have done extensive development planning and engineering in Worcester County and within the Rt 589 corridor. Mr. Cropper asked Mr. Engle if this proposed development conforms with the new land use plan and existing zoning, which Mr. Engle confirmed that it did. Mr. Cropper then asked about engineering feasibility and Mr. Engle answered that it is very feasible to design and construct connections to the Ocean Pines distribution and collection systems for the proposed development in this amendment. Comments were also made about a pump station since the sewer main was a force main and that any designs would conform to County and State standards and would be turned over to the County with appropriate turnover documentation. Ms. Ott wondered if she should recuse herself in light of the fact she lives in the adjacent Ocean Pines Community and owns property in the area of the proposed development. Roscoe Leslie, the County Attorney, commented and reasoned that the appointment of Planning Commissioners by the County Commissions was done in full knowledge of the expertise they bring to the body and that in their decision making they would fairly provide advice and direction on these matters, even if they resided in adjacent properties to the cases they would hear. Comments were also made that recusals are most commonly exercised in those cases where direct and material benefits from decisions could be rendered. Mr. French appreciated the detailed explanations about the case from the applicants and staff. Ms. Purnell and Ms. Ott also echoed those sentiments. Following the discussion, a motion was made by Ms. Knight, seconded by Mr. French, to find this application consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and recommended that they forward a favorable recommendation to the County Commissioners.
